Notice that $-2=(-1)\times 2.$

To raise the product of two numbers to the power of $7$, we can raise each number to the power of $7,$ and then multiply:

$$
(-2)^{7}={((-1)\times 2)}^{7}=(-1)^{7}\times {2}^{7}
$$

Since $-1$ raised to an odd power is $-1,$ we get

$$
(-1)^{7}\times {2}^{7}=(-1)\times {2}^{7}=-{2}^{7}.
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
To raise the product of two numbers to a power, we can raise each number to that power, and then multiply. This is the **power of product rule for exponents**. 

To demonstrate, let's simplify the expression $(5 \times 3)^4$ by applying the power of product rule:

$$
(5\times 3)^4=5^4\times 3^4
$$

**Note:** The power of product rule for exponents is really just a quicker alternative to using repeated multiplication, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5\times 3)^{4} & = \\ {{(5\times 3)\times (5\times 3)\times (5\times 3)\times (5\times 3)}_{⏟}}_{4\text{ copies}} & = \\ {{(5\times 5\times 5\times 5)}_{⏟}}_{4\text{ copies}}\times {{(3\times 3\times 3\times 3)}_{⏟}}_{4\text{ copies}} & = \\ {5}^{4}\times {3}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$
